<title>Getting Started | Guide | Vitest</title>
<location>https://vitest.dev/guide/</location>
<excerpt>Getting Started | Guide | Vitest ## Overview ​ Vitest (pronounced as "veetest") is a next generation testing framework powered by Vite. You can learn more about the rationale behind the project in the Why Vitest section. ## Trying Vitest Online ​ You can try Vitest online on StackBlitz. It runs Vitest directly in the browser, and it is almost identical to the local setup but doesn&`#39`;t require installing anything on your machine. ## Adding Vitest to Your Project ​ ``` npm install -D vitest ``` ``` yarn add -D vitest ``` ``` pnpm add -D vitest ``` ``` bun add -D vitest ``` ``` deno add -D vitest ``` TIP Vitest requires Vite >=v6.4.0 and Node >=v22.12.0 It is recommended that you install a copy of `vitest` in your `package.json`, using one of the methods listed above. However, if you would prefer to run `vitest` directly, you can use `npx vitest` (the `npx` tool comes with npm and Node.js). The `npx` tool will execute the specified command. By default, `npx` will first check if the command exists in the local project&`#39`;s binaries. If it is not found there, `npx` will look in the system&`#39`;s `$PATH` and execute it if found. If the command is not found in either location, `npx` will install it in a temporary location prior to execution. Vitest and third party integrations can use `.vitest` directory to store generated artifacts. It&`#39`;s recommended to add this in your `.gitignore`. .gitignore ``` # Vitest reports and artifacts .vitest/ ``` ## Writing Tests ​ As an example, we will write a simple test that verifies the output of a function that adds two numbers. sum.js ``` export function sum(a, b) { return a + b } ``` sum.test.js ``` import { expect, test } from &`#39`;vitest&`#39`; import { sum } from &`#39`;./sum.js&`#39`; test(&`#39`;adds 1 + 2 to equal 3&`#39`;, () => { expect(sum(1, 2)).toBe(3) }) ``` TIP By default, tests must contain `.test.` or `.spec.` in their file name. Next, in order to execute the test, add the following section to your `package.json`: ``` { "scripts": { "test": "vitest" } } ``` Finally, run `npm run test`, `yarn test` or `pnpm test`, depending on your package manager, and Vitest will print this message: ``` ✓ sum.test.js (1) ✓ adds 1 + 2 to equal 3 Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 1 passed (1) Start at 02:15:44 Duration 311ms ``` WARNING If you are using Bun as your package manager, make sure to use `bun run test` command instead of `bun test`, otherwise Bun will run its own test runner. Your first test is passing! Continue to Writing Tests to learn about organizing tests, reading test output, and the core testing patterns you&`#39`;ll use every day. To run tests once without watching for file changes, use `vitest run`. You can also pass additional flags like `--reporter` or `--coverage`. For a full list of CLI options, run `npx vitest --help` or see the CLI guide. ## Configuring Vitest ​ Vitest reads your `vite.config.*` by default, so your existing Vite plugins and configuration work out-of-the-box. You can also create a dedicated `vitest.config.*` for test-specific settings. See the Config Reference for details. ## IDE Integrations ​ We also provided an official extension for Visual Studio Code to enhance your testing experience with Vitest. ## Examples ​ | Example | Source | Playground | | --- | --- | --- | | `basic` | GitHub | Play Online | | `fastify` | GitHub | Play Online | | `in-source-test` | GitHub | Play Online | | `lit` | GitHub | Play Online | | `vue` | GitHub | Play Online | | `marko` | GitHub | Play Online | | `preact` | GitHub | Play Online | | `qwik` | GitHub | Play Online | | `react` | GitHub | Play Online | | `solid` | GitHub | Play Online | | `svelte` | GitHub | Play Online | | `profiling` | GitHub | Not Available | | `typecheck` | GitHub | Play Online | | `projects` | GitHub | Play Online | Last updated: Jun 18, 2026, 8:04:27 AM</excerpt>

**Raise the Node.js engine floor for packages that run Vitest.** Vitest 5 requires Node.js `>=22.12.0`. `packages/benchmark/package.json` and `packages/storage/package.json` declare Node.js `>=22.5.0` and expose `npm test` scripts that run `vitest run`. On Node.js 22.5–22.11, those commands run Vitest under an unsupported Node version and may fail. CI and publish tests use Bun, but they do not protect this package-level Node path.

Update both package engine ranges to `>=22.12.0` (or the documented Node.js `>=24` floor).
